descriptions.feel: The line carries an emotion the literal wording would not.
descriptions.register: Formality, slang or dialect — who is speaking, and how.
descriptions.metaphor: An image swapped for one that lands in the target culture.
descriptions.prosody: Syllables, stress and breath — how the line sits on the melody.
descriptions.cultural-code: A reference only insiders of the source culture decode.
descriptions.literal-wins: The word-for-word candidate was the strongest and won.
descriptions.form-embedded: Meaning lives in the grammar or the sound, not the words.
descriptions.sung-order: Word order follows the vocal line.
descriptions.onomatopoeia: A sound or ad-lib carried as sung, not translated.
descriptions.idiom-twin: Both languages happen to have the same idiom.
descriptions.false-friend: A look-alike word means something else; the trap was avoided.

home.heroTitle: Hear it. Understand it. Feel it.
home.heroBody: A song in a language you do not speak reaches your ears and stops there. Feelyrics translates the feeling instead of the words, and shows its work: every line carries a note on why it landed that way.

about.title: About Feelyrics
about.leadBody: You play somebody a song that means something to you, in a language they do not speak. They hear a nice melody. Everything that made the song matter stays on your side of the language.
about.answerBody: A literal translation is accurate and empty. Feelyrics goes for the feeling first: it finds the register, the idiom, the cultural code the line is really made of, and rebuilds that in the target language — then writes down why, line by line, so you can disagree with it.
about.rightsBody: Song lyrics are copyrighted, and translating them makes a derivative work. So this site only ever shows two lines of any song, always next to the reasoning that makes them commentary. Full translations exist, but they travel inside personal share links, whose contents never reach this server. Songs whose lyrics are in the public domain are shown in full and say so.
about.communityBody: If a line does not land for you, say how you would land it. No account needed. Accepted corrections change the song for everyone who reads it next — and each one, with its reason tag, becomes a piece of the dataset this project is really building.
about.contact: Questions, corrections and objections are all welcome.
